stem.text: Sodium carbonate neutralises phosphoric acid to produce sodium phosphate, carbon dioxide and water only.
Which volume of 0.50 mol dm<sup>–3</sup> sodium carbonate is needed to exactly neutralise 40.0 cm<sup>3</sup> of 0.25 mol dm<sup>–3</sup> phosphoric acid?

explanation.text: The key step is the balanced equation. Phosphoric acid is H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> and sodium phosphate is Na<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>; each carbonate ion takes two H<sup>+</sup>. Balancing gives 2H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> + 3Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> → 2Na<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> + 3CO<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub>O, so the mole ratio Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> : H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> is 3 : 2.

Moles of H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> = 0.0400 dm<sup>3</sup> × 0.25 mol dm<sup>–3</sup> = 0.0100 mol. Moles of Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> = 0.0100 × 3/2 = 0.0150 mol. Volume = 0.0150 ÷ 0.50 = 0.0300 dm<sup>3</sup> = 30.0 cm<sup>3</sup>.

optionAnalysis.text: Corresponds to 0.00500 mol of Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>, i.e. a 1 : 2 ratio (carbonate : acid), which inverts the 2 : 1 relation between H<sup>+</sup> per acid and H<sup>+</sup> per carbonate.
Corresponds to 0.00667 mol of Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>, i.e. using the 3 : 2 ratio upside down (2/3 instead of 3/2).
Corresponds to a 1 : 1 mole ratio, as if the equation did not need balancing.
Correct. 0.0100 mol H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> needs 0.0150 mol Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>, which is 30.0 cm<sup>3</sup> of a 0.50 mol dm<sup>–3</sup> solution.

inferredMistakes.text: Applying the 3 : 2 ratio the wrong way round and getting 13.3 cm<sup>3</sup>.
Assuming a 1 : 1 ratio without writing the balanced equation and getting 20.0 cm<sup>3</sup>.
